transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah... I came because work has gotten really out of hand. I do bookkeeping, so I'm looking at spreadsheets and calculations all day, and I keep going back over the same ones again and again. Like even after I've already checked them, I’ll think, “Wait, what if I missed something?” and then I have to do it one more time.

Sometimes I stay there for hours after everyone else leaves, which is embarrassing because the cleaning people probably think I’m just slow or something. I mean, my mom always said I was careful with numbers, that’s why I got into this kind of work, but this doesn’t feel like just being careful. It feels like if I don’t check it again, something bad could happen and it would be my fault.
Do you ever have thoughts or mental images that come into your mind uninvited, that you find disturbing or upsetting, and that you try to ignore or suppress?

Yeah… yes, I think that’s exactly what happens. Like I’ll be looking at payroll or tax numbers and even after everything matches, this thought just jumps in, like, what if there’s one hidden mistake I didn’t see? And then someone’s check doesn’t go through, or the firm gets in trouble, and it’s my fault.

I try to tell myself, no, you already looked, it’s fine, but it’s like… I don’t know, it comes right back. Like I can’t trust my own eyes. Even if the spreadsheet is right there in front of me. My old math teacher used to say I had “good attention to detail,” which sounds nice, but this feels different. It’s upsetting, and I try to push it away, but then it just pops back in again.

When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing anything specific — like checking the numbers over and over, or counting, or some kind of routine — to try to make the worry go away or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… mostly checking. I’ll go back over the same spreadsheet or calculation again and again, even if I already checked it and it came out fine. I’ll tell myself, okay, that’s enough, but then I’ll get this feeling like if I don’t look one more time, something bad could happen and it’ll be on me.

Sometimes I stay at work for hours after everyone leaves because I can’t stop going back to it. It’s not like I’m trying to be extra productive. I mean, I used to be the person people asked to double-check things in school, actually, which felt kind of good then… but now it’s just this loop. I check it, feel a little better, then doubt it again.
Do these thoughts and the need to check things over and over cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your life in other ways, like at work or at home?

Yeah… it’s definitely interfering. I mean, I didn’t want to admit that because it sounds like I’m just bad at my job, but I actually missed a filing deadline because I was stuck rechecking other things, and then I got called into this formal meeting at work. Like with my supervisor and everything, not just a quick “hey, be careful.”

And outside work too… I used to go to choir rehearsals, and I’d help at the youth center, but lately I just don’t make it there because I can’t get out of the office on time. I’ll think I’m leaving at six, and then suddenly it’s way later. I used to really like choir, even though I’m not, like, amazing or anything—my friend used to joke I only sing loud on the easy parts—but now I’m missing it because I’m still sitting there checking numbers. So… yeah, it’s causing a lot of problems.
Do you ever feel that the way you check things has to be done in a certain order or a specific way, like if you don’t do it exactly right, you have to start over?

I don’t know if it’s always, like, a perfect order exactly… but I do get stuck doing it a certain way. I’ll go back over the same spreadsheet or the same calculation again and again, and even if I already checked it, I feel like I have to look one more time or something bad could happen and it would be my fault.

Sometimes I’ll be there after everyone else has gone home, just still checking. And then I’m thinking about how the cleaning person probably thinks I’m trying to be really dedicated or something, but I’m not, I’m just… I can’t make myself stop. If I don’t do it right, or if it doesn’t feel right, I end up going back over it again.
Do you ever have thoughts about something bad happening, like someone getting hurt or being in danger, because of a mistake you might have made—even if you know it's unlikely?

Yeah… yes. It’s usually not like I picture some dramatic accident, but I get this thought that I missed one hidden mistake even after the numbers match. Like payroll or taxes—something where if I got it wrong, somebody’s check won’t go through, or the firm could get in trouble.

And I know, logically, if I’ve checked it and it matches, it should be fine. But then my brain is like, “What if you didn’t really see it?” It’s stupid because I’m literally looking right at the numbers, and I still feel like I can’t trust my own eyes. I try to push it away, like, “Stop, you already checked,” but it comes right back. Like maybe there’s one thing I missed hiding in there.

Besides checking numbers or spreadsheets, do you ever find yourself counting, repeating words silently, or doing other specific actions in a certain way to try to reduce your anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Not really counting or repeating words, no… at least I don’t think so. It’s more the checking. Like, I get stuck going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again, even when I already looked at them.

I’ll tell myself, “Okay, you checked it, it’s fine,” and then I’m still sitting there opening it back up or scanning the same rows again. Sometimes everyone else has left work and I’m still there, which is embarrassing because I’m not trying to be some super-dedicated employee or anything. I just feel like if I don’t check it one more time, something bad could happen and it would be my fault.
Have you ever felt the need to count things, repeat certain words silently, or follow other specific routines in a precise way to reduce anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Not really the counting or words thing… I mean, I don’t sit there counting tiles or repeating a phrase in my head. It’s more like I have this routine with the spreadsheets, where I go back over the same rows and calculations again and again.

Sometimes I’ll already know I checked it, but I still reopen it, like, “Just one more time,” and then one more time turns into hours. Everyone else leaves and I’m still there, which is awful because I’m not trying to look hardworking or anything. I just feel like if I don’t check it again, something bad could happen and it would be my fault.

Have you ever felt the need to count objects, repeat certain words silently, or follow other specific routines in a precise way, even if it was just in your head, to reduce anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

No, not really counting objects or saying words in my head… I don’t think I do that. It’s more this exact thing with the spreadsheets. Like I have to go back over the same calculations and rows again, and then again, even after I know I already checked them.

It sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud, but I’ll be at work after everyone else has gone home, and the office is all quiet, and I’m still sitting there thinking, “Just one more time.” And then it’s not one more time. It’s hours. I keep feeling like if I don’t check it again, I’ll miss something and then something bad will happen and it’ll be my fault.
